content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding the 'cycle time for analog value generation' for analog inputs. The inputs on the [product_name] basic module are specified at '300ms', while the [product_name] expansion module shows '50ms'. Should this value be interpreted as the analog-to-digital converter's sampling interval? For example, does '50ms' correspond to 20 samples per second? If so, 20 samples per second appears low for an ADC, which may mean the [product_name] with the expansion module is not suitable for precise real-time analog signal control, such as motor speed or positioning control? [user_name]

Hi, The values of 50ms or 300ms refer to the time required for a single conversion, not the number of conversions per second. You are correct—[product_name] is not intended for real-time analog measurement. For such tasks, it would be better to use a PLC featuring fixed cycle times, interrupts, and higher analog resolution. [product_name] lacks these features and is mainly designed to replace timers and contactors, not for real-time applications. Hope this clarification assists you.

Thank you, [user_name]. If I use [product_name] to operate two relays for controlling a motor in both directions within a 2-meter range at about 0.1m/s, and stop the motor by deactivating relays as the target position is reached: The two analog signals would serve as the set position and feedback from the motor-driven device. In this application, an accuracy of +/- 1 cm is acceptable but I need to understand the precise meaning of '50ms' and the maximum refresh rate of analog inputs on [product_name]. Is it correct that if '50ms' is considered as the sampling interval, the maximum theoretical positioning accuracy would be 0.1m/s * 50ms = 5mm? Thanks again. [user_name]

For a similar application, I used an encoder to provide movement feedback to [product_name] ([article_no]). If input I5 is linked directly to the counter instruction, it's possible to monitor up to 5kHz frequency. In my setup, the motor was connected to a drive with adjustable speed when approaching the target position. I implemented an open-loop, tuned control system and found the results satisfactory for comparable requirements. What are your views on this design approach? [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the analog input cycle time for [product_name] hardware and its relevance to sampling accuracy and real-time control. There is uncertainty whether the stated cycle time relates to sampling rate, affecting both achievable precision and the scope of control applications appropriate for the device. Replies indicate that [product_name] is not intended for high-precision real-time control but is suitable for simpler automation purposes with moderate accuracy needs.
analysis.user_expectations: The user aims to use [product_name] and its expansion module for motor position control and wants to understand the analog input refresh rate to evaluate the feasibility for their precision goal. The user seeks a detailed explanation of the '50ms' analog cycle time and its effect on control accuracy.
